name: Dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE)
lead: Dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE, also dimethylethanolamine, DMEA or deanol) is a colourless amino alcohol with the formula (CH3)2NCH2CH2OH. It is mainly an industrial chemical, used as a curing agent for polyurethanes and epoxy resins and as an intermediate for other compounds. [1][2]

It is also an ingredient in some skin-care products marketed for firming and improving skin tone, and its bitartrate salt is sold as an oral nootropic supplement. [1][2] Wikipedia reports no human trial results for either use, and animal work cited there concerns memory rather than skin. [2] Only one registered human study involving a DMAE-containing skin product was found, and it tested a multi-ingredient combination. [3]
infobox: Bitartrate salt (about 37% DMAE) in supplements; topical cosmetic ingredient [2]

paras: DMAE is a bifunctional molecule carrying a tertiary amine and a primary alcohol. It is prepared industrially by ethoxylation of dimethylamine and is a flammable, corrosive liquid with a fishy odour. [2] Reported oral LD50 in rats is around 1 to 2 g per kg depending on the source. [1][2]

Cosmetic products use DMAE, often as the bitartrate salt at low percentage concentrations, as a skin-firming ingredient. [1] Manufacturers and some proponents describe it as tightening sagging skin and improving tone. [2]

DMAE bitartrate is sold as an oral nootropic. Animal studies cited by Wikipedia suggest possible benefit for spatial and working memory, and a pyroglutamate form has been studied against scopolamine-induced memory deficits. [2]

Concentrated DMAE is classified under GHS as corrosive and acutely toxic by several routes, with hazard statements for skin burns and eye damage. This is an industrial-handling classification and does not directly describe finished cosmetic products. [2][1]
No community discussion was available for this entry. DMAE is listed in the skin category because of its presence in firming cosmetics.

One registered phase 2 study (44 participants, completed 2025) tested a serum and cream combining GABA, DMAE, cysteamine and bakuchiol for skin whitening and anti-aging; because several ingredients were combined, it does not isolate an effect of DMAE. [3] No studies found for DMAE alone in the sources reviewed.

refs.title: Effectiveness of a Bilayering Serum and Cream Containing GABA, DMAE, Cysteamine, and Bakuchiol for Skin Whitening and Anti-Aging

card.summary: Industrial amino alcohol used in skin-firming creams and sold as a nootropic; no human trial isolates its skin effect.
card.note: Concentrated DMAE is a corrosive industrial chemical; cosmetic claims lack published human trials in the sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
DMAE is mostly an industrial chemical used in plastics and resins. It also appears in some firming skin-care products and in oral nootropic supplements.

The sources reviewed report no human trial results for either use, so claims about skin tightening rest on marketing.
quick.mechanism: The way DMAE might affect skin or the brain is not established. Animal studies point to possible memory effects, while no mechanism for skin firming is documented.
quick.risks: The pure liquid is flammable and corrosive and carries hazard warnings. Safety data for cosmetic or supplement use in people are not summarised in the sources reviewed.
